Full solution key — reveal after candidate finishes 
use std::collections::HashMap;

#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq)]
struct VersionedValue {
    value: String,
    version: u64,
}

#[derive(Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
enum StoreError { QuorumUnavailable }

struct Replica {
    is_up: bool,
    store: HashMap<String, VersionedValue>,
}

/// A Dynamo/Cassandra-style tunable-consistency store: `n` replicas total,
/// writes must land on at least `w` of them, reads must hear from at least
/// `r` of them. Callers pass an explicit candidate replica list per call to
/// simulate "which replicas the coordinator happened to reach this time."
struct QuorumStore {
    replicas: Vec<Replica>,
    w: usize,
    r: usize,
}

impl QuorumStore {
    fn new(n: usize, w: usize, r: usize) -> Self {
        let replicas = (0..n).map(|_| Replica { is_up: true, store: HashMap::new() }).collect();
        QuorumStore { replicas, w, r }
    }

    fn set_up(&mut self, idx: usize, up: bool) { self.replicas[idx].is_up = up; }

    /// Writes to the first `w` up replicas found in `candidates`. Checks
    /// reachability BEFORE writing anywhere, so a quorum failure never leaves
    /// a partial write on a subset of replicas — either >= w replicas get the
    /// new version, or NONE of them do.
    fn put(&mut self, candidates: &[usize], key: &str, value: &str, version: u64) -> Result<(), StoreError> {
        let targets: Vec<usize> = candidates.iter().copied().filter(|&idx| self.replicas[idx].is_up).take(self.w).collect();  // decide the full write set BEFORE touching any replica
        if targets.len() < self.w {
            return Err(StoreError::QuorumUnavailable);
        }
        for idx in targets {
            self.replicas[idx].store.insert(key.to_string(), VersionedValue { value: value.to_string(), version });
        }
        Ok(())
    }

    /// Reads from up replicas in `candidates` until `r` responses are collected,
    /// picks the highest-version value among them as the winner, then
    /// READ-REPAIRS: any responding replica whose value was missing or
    /// strictly staler than the winner gets it written back before returning.
    fn get(&mut self, candidates: &[usize], key: &str) -> Result<String, StoreError> {
        let mut responses: Vec<(usize, Option<VersionedValue>)> = Vec::new();
        for &idx in candidates {
            if self.replicas[idx].is_up {
                responses.push((idx, self.replicas[idx].store.get(key).cloned()));
                if responses.len() >= self.r { break; }
            }
        }
        if responses.len() < self.r {
            return Err(StoreError::QuorumUnavailable);
        }

        let winner = responses.iter().filter_map(|(_, v)| v.clone()).max_by_key(|v| v.version);  // HIGHEST version among responses ACTUALLY received wins
        let winner = match winner {
            Some(w) => w,
            None => return Err(StoreError::QuorumUnavailable),
        };

        for (idx, observed) in &responses {
            let is_stale = match observed { Some(v) => v.version < winner.version, None => true };  // missing counts as stale too
            if is_stale {
                self.replicas[*idx].store.insert(key.to_string(), winner.clone());
            }
        }

        Ok(winner.value)
    }
}

fn main() {
    const N: usize = 5;
    const W: usize = 3;
    const R: usize = 3;
    assert!(W + R > N, "W+R>N is the whole point — read-your-writes is not guaranteed otherwise");

    // --- Read-your-writes via the pigeonhole overlap property: a put's W=3
    // write set and a get's R=3 read set are BOTH 3-subsets of only 5
    // replicas, so 3+3=6 > 5 forces them to share at least one replica.
    let put_set = [0usize, 1, 2];
    let read_sets: [[usize; 3]; 3] = [[2, 3, 4], [0, 3, 4], [1, 3, 4]];
    for read_set in read_sets {
        let mut store = QuorumStore::new(N, W, R);
        store.put(&put_set, "k", "just-written", 1).expect("put should succeed with 3 of 3 candidates up");
        let overlap = read_set.iter().any(|idx| put_set.contains(idx));
        assert!(overlap, "test setup bug: read set must overlap put set");
        let value = store.get(&read_set, "k").expect("get should succeed with 3 of 3 candidates up");
        assert_eq!(value, "just-written", "read-your-writes violated for read set {:?}", read_set);
    }

    // --- Read repair must actually mutate a stale replica's STORED data, not
    // just return the right value to the caller.
    let mut store = QuorumStore::new(N, W, R);
    store.put(&[0, 1, 2], "k", "v1", 1).unwrap();
    // Second write only reaches replicas 2,3,4 — replicas 0,1 are left stale.
    store.put(&[2, 3, 4], "k", "v2", 2).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(store.replicas[0].store.get("k").unwrap().version, 1, "replica 0 should still be stale before the read");

    let value = store.get(&[0, 1, 2], "k").expect("get should succeed: 3 of 3 candidates up");
    assert_eq!(value, "v2", "get must return the highest-version value seen");
    assert_eq!(store.replicas[0].store.get("k").unwrap().version, 2, "read repair should have overwritten replica 0's STORED version");  // not just the return value — the replica itself
    assert_eq!(store.replicas[1].store.get("k").unwrap().version, 2, "replica 1 was also stale and read from, so it must be repaired too");

    // --- Availability: with exactly N-W (or N-R) replicas down, operations
    // still succeed using the remaining replicas that exactly meet quorum.
    let mut store = QuorumStore::new(N, W, R);
    store.set_up(3, false);
    store.set_up(4, false);
    store.put(&[0, 1, 2], "k", "survives-2-down", 1).expect("put should succeed with exactly W=3 replicas up");
    let value = store.get(&[0, 1, 2], "k").expect("get should succeed with exactly R=3 replicas up");
    assert_eq!(value, "survives-2-down");

    // --- But with only 2 replicas up (one below quorum), operations must
    // fail loudly instead of silently succeeding with insufficient replicas.
    store.set_up(2, false);
    let put_result = store.put(&[0, 1, 2], "k", "should-not-land", 2);
    assert_eq!(put_result, Err(StoreError::QuorumUnavailable), "put with only 2 of 3 needed replicas up must fail");
    let get_result = store.get(&[0, 1, 2], "k");
    assert_eq!(get_result, Err(StoreError::QuorumUnavailable), "get with only 2 of 3 needed replicas up must fail");
    // And the earlier successful write must be untouched by the failed attempt.
    assert_eq!(store.replicas[0].store.get("k").unwrap().value, "survives-2-down");

    println!("quorum read/write test passed: N={}, W={}, R={}", N, W, R);
}
What to look for — unprompted signals
  • ★★★Decides the full write (or read) set BEFORE mutating anything — a candidate who writes to each candidate replica as they iterate, checking the quorum count only at the very end, will leave real partial writes on disk the moment the loop runs out of up-replicas before reaching w; that under-quorum "successful" partial write is a genuine, silent correctness bug (a client is told the write failed, but some replicas now disagree with the value that existed before the attempt), not just an implementation-style nit.
  • ★★★Picks the winning value by comparing the VERSION of responses actually received, not by any positional or "first response" heuristic — a candidate who returns e.g. the first successful response instead of computing max_by_key(version) across the whole read set will pass a lucky test ordering and then silently violate read-your-writes the moment the read quorum happens to contact a stale replica before a fresh one.
  • ★★★Read repair mutates the REPLICA's own stored state, not just a local copy used to compute the return value — this is exactly why the test asserts the replica's store map directly rather than only checking get()'s return value; a candidate who computes the winner correctly but forgets (or is too lazy) to write it back to the stale replicas has implemented "read resolution" but not "read REPAIR," and the system's total staleness never actually improves over time.
  • ★★Can immediately justify W + R > N via the pigeonhole principle without hand-waving — any W-sized write set and any R-sized read set are both subsets of the same N replicas, and W + R > N is exactly the arithmetic condition under which two subsets of sizes W and R drawn from a universe of size N are FORCED to intersect; a candidate who can't explain this and instead says something like "because it's a majority" is reciting a rule they haven't actually derived.
Follow-up probes
  • P1"You're using a bare version number for conflict resolution — what's the problem with that in a real multi-writer system, and what would Dynamo actually use instead?" — A simple incrementing version number requires a single source of truth for "the next version," which doesn't exist in a system with multiple concurrent writers and no coordinator; real Dynamo-style systems use per-key VECTOR CLOCKS (see the vector-clocks exercise) precisely so two concurrent writes can be recognized as CONCURRENT rather than one arbitrarily "winning" by version number — this exercise's simple version-number LWW is a deliberate simplification of what Dynamo/Cassandra call "timestamp-based reconciliation," one of several reconciliation strategies, chosen here specifically to keep the quorum-overlap mechanics the focus.
  • P2"Read repair fixes staleness only for keys that happen to get READ — what fixes replicas that just silently drift and are never read again?" — This is exactly what Dynamo calls anti-entropy via Merkle trees, or "hinted handoff" combined with a periodic full-replica repair process (Cassandra's nodetool repair) — a background process that proactively compares replica digests and reconciles differences even for cold keys, complementing read repair's purely reactive, read-triggered fix-up.
  • P3"What consistency level would you pick for W and R if you wanted STRONG consistency instead of just read-your-writes, and what do you give up?" — Setting W = N (write to every replica) or R = N (read from every replica) gets you strict linearizable-style consistency for that operation type, but at the direct cost of availability: with W = N, a SINGLE down replica blocks every write, which is precisely the CAP-theorem trade-off Dynamo's tunable N/W/R knobs are designed to let an operator choose per-use-case rather than have baked into the system.
🎯 Senior angle
A mid-level candidate treats W + R > N as a rule to apply. A senior candidate treats it as arithmetic they can re-derive on a whiteboard in ten seconds — and, more importantly, immediately spots that read repair only helps keys that get read, which is exactly the gap real systems close with a SEPARATE, proactive anti-entropy/Merkle-tree repair process. Naming that gap unprompted, and knowing it's a distinct mechanism from read repair rather than "the same thing," is the difference between having implemented Dynamo's quorum mechanics and having actually understood why Dynamo also needs nodetool repair.

    // use: VersionedValue, Replica, QuorumStore
    todo!()
}

fn main() {
    // Harden · Decides the full write (or read) set BEFORE mutating anyt…
    harden_w83_4();
    // Parent exercise still holds after the harden change:
    const N: usize = 5;
    const W: usize = 3;
    const R: usize = 3;
    assert!(W + R > N, "W+R>N is the whole point — read-your-writes is not guaranteed otherwise");

    // --- Read-your-writes via the pigeonhole overlap property: a put's W=3
    // write set and a get's R=3 read set are BOTH 3-subsets of only 5
    // replicas, so 3+3=6 > 5 forces them to share at least one replica.
    let put_set = [0usize, 1, 2];
    let read_sets: [[usize; 3]; 3] = [[2, 3, 4], [0, 3, 4], [1, 3, 4]];
    for read_set in read_sets {
        let mut store = QuorumStore::new(N, W, R);
        store.put(&put_set, "k", "just-written", 1).expect("put should succeed with 3 of 3 candidates up");
        let overlap = read_set.iter().any(|idx| put_set.contains(idx));
        assert!(overlap, "test setup bug: read set must overlap put set");
        let value = store.get(&read_set, "k").expect("get should succeed with 3 of 3 candidates up");
        assert_eq!(value, "just-written", "read-your-writes violated for read set {:?}", read_set);
    }

    // --- Read repair must actually mutate a stale replica's STORED data, not
    // just return the right value to the caller.
    let mut store = QuorumStore::new(N, W, R);
    store.put(&[0, 1, 2], "k", "v1", 1).unwrap();
    // Second write only reaches replicas 2,3,4 — replicas 0,1 are left stale.
    store.put(&[2, 3, 4], "k", "v2", 2).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(store.replicas[0].store.get("k").unwrap().version, 1, "replica 0 should still be stale before the read");

    let value = store.get(&[0, 1, 2], "k").expect("get should succeed: 3 of 3 candidates up");
    assert_eq!(value, "v2", "get must return the highest-version value seen");
    assert_eq!(store.replicas[0].store.get("k").unwrap().version, 2, "read repair should have overwritten replica 0's STORED version");  // not just the return value — the replica itself
    assert_eq!(store.replicas[1].store.get("k").unwrap().version, 2, "replica 1 was also stale and read from, so it must be repaired too");

    // --- Availability: with exactly N-W (or N-R) replicas down, operations
    // still succeed using the remaining replicas that exactly meet quorum.
    let mut store = QuorumStore::new(N, W, R);
    store.set_up(3, false);
    store.set_up(4, false);
    store.put(&[0, 1, 2], "k", "survives-2-down", 1).expect("put should succeed with exactly W=3 replicas up");
    let value = store.get(&[0, 1, 2], "k").expect("get should succeed with exactly R=3 replicas up");
    assert_eq!(value, "survives-2-down");

    // --- But with only 2 replicas up (one below quorum), operations must
    // fail loudly instead of silently succeeding with insufficient replicas.
    store.set_up(2, false);
    let put_result = store.put(&[0, 1, 2], "k", "should-not-land", 2);
    assert_eq!(put_result, Err(StoreError::QuorumUnavailable), "put with only 2 of 3 needed replicas up must fail");
    let get_result = store.get(&[0, 1, 2], "k");
    assert_eq!(get_result, Err(StoreError::QuorumUnavailable), "get with only 2 of 3 needed replicas up must fail");
    // And the earlier successful write must be untouched by the failed attempt.
    assert_eq!(store.replicas[0].store.get("k").unwrap().value, "survives-2-down");

    println!("quorum read/write test passed: N={}, W={}, R={}", N, W, R);
}

// Systems Exercise 84 · 40 min
W84 · Snowflake ID Generator
distributed-id bit-packing clock-skew injected-clock Medium
Prompt
"Implement a Twitter-style Snowflake ID generator: 41-bit timestamp | 10-bit worker_id | 12-bit sequence. next_id(now_ms) must be unique and roughly time-ordered. Handle clock skew (return an error if time went backwards) and sequence exhaustion within a millisecond (error or wait-until-next-ms helper). Inject the clock — no Instant::now() inside the generator — so the logic is unit-testable."
Starter code to hand to candidate
#[derive(Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
enum SnowflakeError {
    ClockWentBackwards { last: u64, now: u64 },
    SequenceExhausted,
}

struct Snowflake {
    worker_id: u16, // 10 bits
    epoch_ms: u64,
    last_ms: u64,
    seq: u16, // 12 bits
}

impl Snowflake {
    fn new(worker_id: u16, epoch_ms: u64) -> Self { todo!() }
    fn next_id(&mut self, now_ms: u64) -> Result<u64, SnowflakeError> { todo!() }
    fn next_id_wait<F: FnMut() -> u64>(&mut self, clock: F) -> Result<u64, SnowflakeError> { todo!() }
    fn unpack(id: u64) -> (u64, u16, u16) { todo!() }
}


fn main() {
    let mut gen = Snowflake::new(7, 1_600_000_000_000);
    let a = gen.next_id(1_600_000_000_100).unwrap();
    let b = gen.next_id(1_600_000_000_100).unwrap();
    assert_ne!(a, b);
    let (ts_a, w_a, s_a) = Snowflake::unpack(a);
    let (ts_b, w_b, s_b) = Snowflake::unpack(b);
    assert_eq!(ts_a, 100);
    assert_eq!(ts_b, 100);
    assert_eq!(w_a, 7);
    assert_eq!(w_b, 7);
    assert_eq!(s_a, 0);
    assert_eq!(s_b, 1);

    // New millisecond resets sequence
    let c = gen.next_id(1_600_000_000_101).unwrap();
    let (_, _, s_c) = Snowflake::unpack(c);
    assert_eq!(s_c, 0);

    // Clock skew
    assert_eq!(
        gen.next_id(1_600_000_000_050),
        Err(SnowflakeError::ClockWentBackwards { last: 101, now: 50 })
    );

    // Exhaust 4096 ids in one ms
    let mut g2 = Snowflake::new(1, 0);
    for i in 0..4096u16 {
        let id = g2.next_id(1000).unwrap();
        let (_, _, s) = Snowflake::unpack(id);
        assert_eq!(s, i);
    }
    assert_eq!(g2.next_id(1000), Err(SnowflakeError::SequenceExhausted));

    // Wait helper advances when clock ticks
    let mut tick = 1000u64;
    let id = g2
        .next_id_wait(|| {
            tick += 1;
            tick
        })
        .unwrap();
    let (ts, _, s) = Snowflake::unpack(id);
    assert_eq!(ts, 1001);
    assert_eq!(s, 0);

    println!("W84 ok");
}
Full solution key — reveal after candidate finishes 
#[derive(Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
enum SnowflakeError {
    ClockWentBackwards { last: u64, now: u64 },
    SequenceExhausted,
}

struct Snowflake {
    worker_id: u16, // 10 bits
    epoch_ms: u64,
    last_ms: u64,
    seq: u16, // 12 bits
}

impl Snowflake {
    fn new(worker_id: u16, epoch_ms: u64) -> Self {
        assert!(worker_id < 1024, "worker_id must fit in 10 bits");
        Self {
            worker_id,
            epoch_ms,
            last_ms: 0,
            seq: 0,
        }
    }

    /// Injected clock — no Instant::now() inside next_id for testability.
    fn next_id(&mut self, now_ms: u64) -> Result<u64, SnowflakeError> {
        let ts = now_ms.saturating_sub(self.epoch_ms);
        if ts < self.last_ms {
            return Err(SnowflakeError::ClockWentBackwards {
                last: self.last_ms,
                now: ts,
            });
        }
        if ts == self.last_ms {
            self.seq = (self.seq + 1) & 0x0FFF;
            if self.seq == 0 {
                // Sequence exhausted in this millisecond — wait for next ms (caller injects).
                return Err(SnowflakeError::SequenceExhausted);
            }
        } else {
            self.seq = 0;
            self.last_ms = ts;
        }
        // Pack: [41 ts][10 worker][12 seq]
        Ok(((ts & 0x1FF_FFFF_FFFF) << 22) | ((self.worker_id as u64 & 0x3FF) << 12) | (self.seq as u64))
    }

    /// Busy-wait helper for SequenceExhausted: advance until clock moves.
    fn next_id_wait<F: FnMut() -> u64>(&mut self, mut clock: F) -> Result<u64, SnowflakeError> {
        loop {
            match self.next_id(clock()) {
                Err(SnowflakeError::SequenceExhausted) => continue,
                other => return other,
            }
        }
    }

    fn unpack(id: u64) -> (u64, u16, u16) {
        let seq = (id & 0x0FFF) as u16;
        let worker = ((id >> 12) & 0x3FF) as u16;
        let ts = (id >> 22) & 0x1FF_FFFF_FFFF;
        (ts, worker, seq)
    }
}

fn main() {
    let mut gen = Snowflake::new(7, 1_600_000_000_000);
    let a = gen.next_id(1_600_000_000_100).unwrap();
    let b = gen.next_id(1_600_000_000_100).unwrap();
    assert_ne!(a, b);
    let (ts_a, w_a, s_a) = Snowflake::unpack(a);
    let (ts_b, w_b, s_b) = Snowflake::unpack(b);
    assert_eq!(ts_a, 100);
    assert_eq!(ts_b, 100);
    assert_eq!(w_a, 7);
    assert_eq!(w_b, 7);
    assert_eq!(s_a, 0);
    assert_eq!(s_b, 1);

    // New millisecond resets sequence
    let c = gen.next_id(1_600_000_000_101).unwrap();
    let (_, _, s_c) = Snowflake::unpack(c);
    assert_eq!(s_c, 0);

    // Clock skew
    assert_eq!(
        gen.next_id(1_600_000_000_050),
        Err(SnowflakeError::ClockWentBackwards { last: 101, now: 50 })
    );

    // Exhaust 4096 ids in one ms
    let mut g2 = Snowflake::new(1, 0);
    for i in 0..4096u16 {
        let id = g2.next_id(1000).unwrap();
        let (_, _, s) = Snowflake::unpack(id);
        assert_eq!(s, i);
    }
    assert_eq!(g2.next_id(1000), Err(SnowflakeError::SequenceExhausted));

    // Wait helper advances when clock ticks
    let mut tick = 1000u64;
    let id = g2
        .next_id_wait(|| {
            tick += 1;
            tick
        })
        .unwrap();
    let (ts, _, s) = Snowflake::unpack(id);
    assert_eq!(ts, 1001);
    assert_eq!(s, 0);

    println!("W84 ok");
}
What to look for — unprompted signals
  • ★★★Injects the clock and treats backwards time as an explicit error rather than silently minting duplicate or out-of-order IDs.
  • ★★★Caps sequence at 12 bits and surfaces exhaustion (wait or error) instead of wrapping into collisions.
  • ★★Packs bits correctly (ts << 22 | worker << 12 | seq) and can unpack for debugging.
  • ★Uses integer milliseconds from a custom epoch — no floats, no system clock inside the core.
Follow-up probes
  • P1"What breaks if two workers share a worker_id?" — ID collisions across machines. Worker assignment must be unique (config, ZooKeeper, etc.).
  • P2"Why not use UUID v4?" — UUIDs are not time-sortable and are 128-bit; Snowflake gives locality for DB indexes and ~64-bit ids.
  • P3"How would you make this lock-free under concurrency?" — Per-thread/per-shard generators with distinct worker bits, or atomic CAS on (last_ms, seq) packed state.
🎯 Senior angle
The interview signal is clock discipline: injected time, monotonicity checks, and an explicit policy when the sequence space is exhausted. Candidates who call SystemTime::now() inside next_id and ignore skew usually fail the production follow-ups.

    assert_eq!(s_c, 0);

    // Clock skew
    assert_eq!(
        gen.next_id(1_600_000_000_050),
        Err(SnowflakeError::ClockWentBackwards { last: 101, now: 50 })
    );

    // Exhaust 4096 ids in one ms
    let mut g2 = Snowflake::new(1, 0);
    for i in 0..4096u16 {
        let id = g2.next_id(1000).unwrap();
        let (_, _, s) = Snowflake::unpack(id);
        assert_eq!(s, i);
    }
    assert_eq!(g2.next_id(1000), Err(SnowflakeError::SequenceExhausted));

    // Wait helper advances when clock ticks
    let mut tick = 1000u64;
    let id = g2
        .next_id_wait(|| {
            tick += 1;
            tick
        })
        .unwrap();
    let (ts, _, s) = Snowflake::unpack(id);
    assert_eq!(ts, 1001);
    assert_eq!(s, 0);

    println!("W84 ok");
}

W85 · Consistent Hashing Ring
consistent-hash virtual-nodes BTreeMap minimal-remapping Medium
Prompt
"Build a consistent hashing ring with virtual nodes. Support add_node, remove_node, and lookup(key) -> node (clockwise successor, wrap around). Demonstrate minimal remapping: when a node leaves, only keys that hashed to it move; keys on other nodes stay put. Std-only hash is fine (FNV/SipHash-style)."
Starter code to hand to candidate
use std::collections::BTreeMap;

struct HashRing {
    ring: BTreeMap<u64, String>,
    vnodes: u32,
}

impl HashRing {
    fn new(vnodes: u32) -> Self { todo!() }
    fn add_node(&mut self, name: &str) { todo!() }
    fn remove_node(&mut self, name: &str) { todo!() }
    fn lookup(&self, key: &str) -> Option<&str> { todo!() }
}


fn main() {
    let mut ring = HashRing::new(50);
    ring.add_node("A");
    ring.add_node("B");
    ring.add_node("C");

    // Mix key shapes so FNV doesn't clump them into one arc
    let keys: Vec<String> = (0u32..2000)
        .map(|i| format!("user:{i}/session:{}", i.wrapping_mul(2654435761)))
        .collect();
    let before: Vec<String> = keys
        .iter()
        .map(|k| ring.lookup(k).unwrap().to_string())
        .collect();
    let on_a = before.iter().filter(|n| *n == "A").count();
    let on_b = before.iter().filter(|n| *n == "B").count();
    let on_c = before.iter().filter(|n| *n == "C").count();
    assert!(on_a > 0 && on_b > 0 && on_c > 0, "expected keys on all nodes: {on_a}/{on_b}/{on_c}");

    // Removing B should remap only keys that were on B (minimal remapping)
    ring.remove_node("B");
    let after: Vec<String> = keys
        .iter()
        .map(|k| ring.lookup(k).unwrap().to_string())
        .collect();

    let mut remapped = 0usize;
    let mut stayed_on_non_b = 0usize;
    for i in 0..keys.len() {
        if before[i] == "B" {
            assert_ne!(after[i], "B");
            remapped += 1;
        } else {
            // Keys that were on A or C should stay put when B leaves
            assert_eq!(before[i], after[i], "key {} remapped unnecessarily", keys[i]);
            stayed_on_non_b += 1;
        }
    }
    assert_eq!(remapped, on_b);
    assert!(stayed_on_non_b > 0);

    // Adding D redistributes some keys but not all
    let mid: Vec<String> = keys
        .iter()
        .map(|k| ring.lookup(k).unwrap().to_string())
        .collect();
    ring.add_node("D");
    let mut moved_to_d = 0usize;
    let mut unchanged = 0usize;
    for (i, k) in keys.iter().enumerate() {
        let now = ring.lookup(k).unwrap();
        if now == "D" {
            moved_to_d += 1;
        } else if now == mid[i] {
            unchanged += 1;
        }
    }
    assert!(moved_to_d > 0);
    assert!(unchanged > 0);
    assert!(ring.lookup("anything").is_some());

    println!("W85 ok: remapped_from_B={remapped} moved_to_D={moved_to_d}");
}
Full solution key — reveal after candidate finishes 
use std::collections::BTreeMap;

struct HashRing {
    /// hash → physical node name
    ring: BTreeMap<u64, String>,
    vnodes: u32,
}

impl HashRing {
    fn new(vnodes: u32) -> Self {
        assert!(vnodes > 0);
        Self {
            ring: BTreeMap::new(),
            vnodes,
        }
    }

    fn hash(bytes: &[u8]) -> u64 {
        // FNV-1a 64-bit — good enough for interview ring placement
        let mut h: u64 = 0xcbf29ce484222325;
        for &b in bytes {
            h ^= b as u64;
            h = h.wrapping_mul(0x100000001b3);
        }
        h
    }

    fn add_node(&mut self, name: &str) {
        for i in 0..self.vnodes {
            let key = format!("{name}#{i}");
            self.ring.insert(Self::hash(key.as_bytes()), name.to_string());
        }
    }

    fn remove_node(&mut self, name: &str) {
        self.ring.retain(|_, n| n != name);
    }

    fn lookup(&self, key: &str) -> Option<&str> {
        if self.ring.is_empty() {
            return None;
        }
        let h = Self::hash(key.as_bytes());
        // clockwise: first vnode at or after h, else wrap to first
        if let Some((_, node)) = self.ring.range(h..).next() {
            Some(node.as_str())
        } else {
            self.ring.values().next().map(|s| s.as_str())
        }
    }
}

fn main() {
    let mut ring = HashRing::new(50);
    ring.add_node("A");
    ring.add_node("B");
    ring.add_node("C");

    // Mix key shapes so FNV doesn't clump them into one arc
    let keys: Vec<String> = (0u32..2000)
        .map(|i| format!("user:{i}/session:{}", i.wrapping_mul(2654435761)))
        .collect();
    let before: Vec<String> = keys
        .iter()
        .map(|k| ring.lookup(k).unwrap().to_string())
        .collect();
    let on_a = before.iter().filter(|n| *n == "A").count();
    let on_b = before.iter().filter(|n| *n == "B").count();
    let on_c = before.iter().filter(|n| *n == "C").count();
    assert!(on_a > 0 && on_b > 0 && on_c > 0, "expected keys on all nodes: {on_a}/{on_b}/{on_c}");

    // Removing B should remap only keys that were on B (minimal remapping)
    ring.remove_node("B");
    let after: Vec<String> = keys
        .iter()
        .map(|k| ring.lookup(k).unwrap().to_string())
        .collect();

    let mut remapped = 0usize;
    let mut stayed_on_non_b = 0usize;
    for i in 0..keys.len() {
        if before[i] == "B" {
            assert_ne!(after[i], "B");
            remapped += 1;
        } else {
            // Keys that were on A or C should stay put when B leaves
            assert_eq!(before[i], after[i], "key {} remapped unnecessarily", keys[i]);
            stayed_on_non_b += 1;
        }
    }
    assert_eq!(remapped, on_b);
    assert!(stayed_on_non_b > 0);

    // Adding D redistributes some keys but not all
    let mid: Vec<String> = keys
        .iter()
        .map(|k| ring.lookup(k).unwrap().to_string())
        .collect();
    ring.add_node("D");
    let mut moved_to_d = 0usize;
    let mut unchanged = 0usize;
    for (i, k) in keys.iter().enumerate() {
        let now = ring.lookup(k).unwrap();
        if now == "D" {
            moved_to_d += 1;
        } else if now == mid[i] {
            unchanged += 1;
        }
    }
    assert!(moved_to_d > 0);
    assert!(unchanged > 0);
    assert!(ring.lookup("anything").is_some());

    println!("W85 ok: remapped_from_B={remapped} moved_to_D={moved_to_d}");
}
What to look for — unprompted signals
  • ★★★Virtual nodes per physical node — without them the ring is badly unbalanced.
  • ★★★Proves minimal remapping with an assert, not just a verbal claim.
  • ★★BTreeMap range + wrap for O(log n) clockwise lookup.
  • ★Mentions that real systems often use jump/rendezvous hashing or Maglev for better balance.
Follow-up probes
  • P1"How many vnodes?" — Trade memory vs balance; hundreds per node is common. Measure load stddev.
  • P2"What about hot keys?" — Consistent hashing does not fix skew on a single key; need key sharding or caching.
  • P3"Replication?" — Walk clockwise for N distinct physical successors (skip sibling vnodes of same node).
🎯 Senior angle
Consistent hashing interviews separate people who can sketch a circle from people who can measure remapping. Senior angle: vnode count, hash quality, and what happens under correlated key spaces.

    assert!(on_a > 0 && on_b > 0 && on_c > 0, "expected keys on all nodes: {on_a}/{on_b}/{on_c}");

    // Removing B should remap only keys that were on B (minimal remapping)
    ring.remove_node("B");
    let after: Vec<String> = keys
        .iter()
        .map(|k| ring.lookup(k).unwrap().to_string())
        .collect();

    let mut remapped = 0usize;
    let mut stayed_on_non_b = 0usize;
    for i in 0..keys.len() {
        if before[i] == "B" {
            assert_ne!(after[i], "B");
            remapped += 1;
        } else {
            // Keys that were on A or C should stay put when B leaves
            assert_eq!(before[i], after[i], "key {} remapped unnecessarily", keys[i]);
            stayed_on_non_b += 1;
        }
    }
    assert_eq!(remapped, on_b);
    assert!(stayed_on_non_b > 0);

    // Adding D redistributes some keys but not all
    let mid: Vec<String> = keys
        .iter()
        .map(|k| ring.lookup(k).unwrap().to_string())
        .collect();
    ring.add_node("D");
    let mut moved_to_d = 0usize;
    let mut unchanged = 0usize;
    for (i, k) in keys.iter().enumerate() {
        let now = ring.lookup(k).unwrap();
        if now == "D" {
            moved_to_d += 1;
        } else if now == mid[i] {
            unchanged += 1;
        }
    }
    assert!(moved_to_d > 0);
    assert!(unchanged > 0);
    assert!(ring.lookup("anything").is_some());

    println!("W85 ok: remapped_from_B={remapped} moved_to_D={moved_to_d}");
}

        Err(LeaseError::StaleFence {
            presented: 1,
            current: 2
        })
    );
    assert!(mgr.write("bob", b.fence, 1650, b"fresh").is_ok());

    // Expired lease rejects writes
    assert_eq!(mgr.write("bob", b.fence, 2200, b"late"), Err(LeaseError::Expired));

    println!("W86 ok");

Full solution key — reveal after candidate finishes 
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
struct Lease {
    owner: String,
    fence: u64,
    expires_at_ms: u64,
}

#[derive(Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
enum LeaseError {
    HeldByOther,
    StaleFence { presented: u64, current: u64 },
    Expired,
    NotHeld,
}

struct LeaseManager {
    current: Option<Lease>,
    next_fence: u64,
}

impl LeaseManager {
    fn new() -> Self {
        Self {
            current: None,
            next_fence: 1,
        }
    }

    fn grant(&mut self, owner: &str, now_ms: u64, ttl_ms: u64) -> Result<Lease, LeaseError> {
        if let Some(ref l) = self.current {
            if l.expires_at_ms > now_ms && l.owner != owner {
                return Err(LeaseError::HeldByOther);
            }
        }
        let lease = Lease {
            owner: owner.to_string(),
            fence: self.next_fence,
            expires_at_ms: now_ms + ttl_ms,
        };
        self.next_fence += 1;
        self.current = Some(lease.clone());
        Ok(lease)
    }

    /// Storage write guarded by fencing token. Must present fence ≥ current.
    fn write(&mut self, owner: &str, fence: u64, now_ms: u64, _payload: &[u8]) -> Result<(), LeaseError> {
        let Some(ref lease) = self.current else {
            return Err(LeaseError::NotHeld);
        };
        if lease.expires_at_ms <= now_ms {
            return Err(LeaseError::Expired);
        }
        if lease.owner != owner {
            return Err(LeaseError::HeldByOther);
        }
        if fence < lease.fence {
            return Err(LeaseError::StaleFence {
                presented: fence,
                current: lease.fence,
            });
        }
        Ok(())
    }
}

fn main() {
    let mut mgr = LeaseManager::new();
    let a = mgr.grant("alice", 1000, 500).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(a.fence, 1);
    assert!(mgr.write("alice", a.fence, 1100, b"ok").is_ok());

    // Bob cannot steal while lease is live
    assert_eq!(mgr.grant("bob", 1200, 500), Err(LeaseError::HeldByOther));

    // After expiry Bob can take over with a higher fence
    let b = mgr.grant("bob", 1600, 500).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(b.fence, 2);

    // Alice's stale fence is rejected even if she retries
    assert_eq!(
        mgr.write("alice", a.fence, 1650, b"stale"),
        Err(LeaseError::HeldByOther)
    );
    assert_eq!(
        mgr.write("bob", a.fence, 1650, b"wrong fence"),
        Err(LeaseError::StaleFence {
            presented: 1,
            current: 2
        })
    );
    assert!(mgr.write("bob", b.fence, 1650, b"fresh").is_ok());

    // Expired lease rejects writes
    assert_eq!(mgr.write("bob", b.fence, 2200, b"late"), Err(LeaseError::Expired));

    println!("W86 ok");
}
What to look for — unprompted signals
  • ★★★Monotonic fence increments on every successful grant — never reused.
  • ★★★Storage rejects fence < current even if the caller still has an old lease object.
  • ★★TTL checked on write with injected clock — expired lease cannot mutate.
  • ★Can name ZooKeeper zxid / etcd mod_revision / Redlock fencing as the real-world analogue.
Follow-up probes
  • P1"Why is TTL alone insufficient?" — GC pauses / GC clocks let a zombie wake after expiry and write; fence makes storage ignore it.
  • P2"Where must the fence be checked?" — At the storage/resource side, not only at the lock service.
  • P3"Clock sync?" — Lease expiry needs roughly synced clocks or a central time authority; fencing still protects against zombies.
🎯 Senior angle
Fencing tokens are the answer to “what if the lock holder GC-pauses past expiry?” Watch for candidates who only check ownership strings and never a monotonic epoch — that design loses to split-brain every time.

W87 · Idempotency-Key Store

Prompt
"Build an in-memory idempotency-key store for HTTP APIs. begin(key) returns Fresh(handle) | ReplayInFlight(handle) | ReplayCompleted(handle, response). In-flight duplicates must share the same handle; completed keys return the stored response without re-executing. complete(key, handle, response) transitions InFlight → Completed."
Starter code to hand to candidate

    Fresh { handle: u64 },
    ReplayInFlight { handle: u64 },
    ReplayCompleted { handle: u64, response: String },
}

struct IdempotencyStore { /* map key -> InFlight|Completed */ }

impl IdempotencyStore {
    fn new() -> Self { todo!() }
    fn begin(&mut self, key: &str) -> BeginResult { todo!() }
    fn complete(&mut self, key: &str, handle: u64, response: String) -> Result<(), &'static str> { todo!() }
}


fn main() {
    let mut store = IdempotencyStore::new();

    match store.begin("pay-1") {
        BeginResult::Fresh { handle } => {
            assert_eq!(handle, 1);
            // Duplicate while in-flight returns same handle
            assert_eq!(
                store.begin("pay-1"),
                BeginResult::ReplayInFlight { handle: 1 }
            );
            store.complete("pay-1", 1, r#"{"ok":true}"#.into()).unwrap();
        }
        _ => panic!("expected Fresh"),
    }

    // Completed key replays stored response
    assert_eq!(
        store.begin("pay-1"),
        BeginResult::ReplayCompleted {
            handle: 1,
            response: r#"{"ok":true}"#.into()
        }
    );

    // Different key is independent
    assert_eq!(store.begin("pay-2"), BeginResult::Fresh { handle: 2 });

    println!("W87 ok");
}
Full solution key — reveal after candidate finishes 
use std::collections::HashMap;

#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
enum Record {
    InFlight { handle: u64 },
    Completed { handle: u64, response: String },
}

#[derive(Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
enum BeginResult {
    Fresh { handle: u64 },
    ReplayInFlight { handle: u64 },
    ReplayCompleted { handle: u64, response: String },
}

struct IdempotencyStore {
    map: HashMap<String, Record>,
    next_handle: u64,
}

impl IdempotencyStore {
    fn new() -> Self {
        Self {
            map: HashMap::new(),
            next_handle: 1,
        }
    }

    fn begin(&mut self, key: &str) -> BeginResult {
        match self.map.get(key) {
            Some(Record::InFlight { handle }) => BeginResult::ReplayInFlight { handle: *handle },
            Some(Record::Completed { handle, response }) => BeginResult::ReplayCompleted {
                handle: *handle,
                response: response.clone(),
            },
            None => {
                let handle = self.next_handle;
                self.next_handle += 1;
                self.map.insert(key.to_string(), Record::InFlight { handle });
                BeginResult::Fresh { handle }
            }
        }
    }

    fn complete(&mut self, key: &str, handle: u64, response: String) -> Result<(), &'static str> {
        match self.map.get(key) {
            Some(Record::InFlight { handle: h }) if *h == handle => {
                self.map.insert(
                    key.to_string(),
                    Record::Completed {
                        handle,
                        response,
                    },
                );
                Ok(())
            }
            Some(Record::Completed { handle: h, .. }) if *h == handle => Ok(()), // already done
            _ => Err("unknown or mismatched handle"),
        }
    }
}

fn main() {
    let mut store = IdempotencyStore::new();

    match store.begin("pay-1") {
        BeginResult::Fresh { handle } => {
            assert_eq!(handle, 1);
            // Duplicate while in-flight returns same handle
            assert_eq!(
                store.begin("pay-1"),
                BeginResult::ReplayInFlight { handle: 1 }
            );
            store.complete("pay-1", 1, r#"{"ok":true}"#.into()).unwrap();
        }
        _ => panic!("expected Fresh"),
    }

    // Completed key replays stored response
    assert_eq!(
        store.begin("pay-1"),
        BeginResult::ReplayCompleted {
            handle: 1,
            response: r#"{"ok":true}"#.into()
        }
    );

    // Different key is independent
    assert_eq!(store.begin("pay-2"), BeginResult::Fresh { handle: 2 });

    println!("W87 ok");
}
What to look for — unprompted signals
  • ★★★Three-way begin result — Fresh / InFlight / Completed — not a boolean.
  • ★★★Completed replay returns stored response — side effects do not re-run.
  • ★★Handle mismatch on complete is rejected — prevents completing someone else's request.
  • ★Mentions TTL/expiry and fingerprinting request body in production.
Follow-up probes
  • P1"Client retries while first request still running — what should happen?" — Same in-flight handle; optionally wait/long-poll, never start a second charge.
  • P2"What if begin and complete are on different replicas?" — Needs shared store (Redis/DB) with atomic compare-and-set on key state.
  • P3"Should the key cover the request body?" — Yes: same key + different body is usually 409 Conflict.
🎯 Senior angle
Idempotency is a state machine, not a cache. Seniors model InFlight vs Completed explicitly and talk about request fingerprints, TTLs, and cross-replica atomicity — not just HashMap<String, String>.

Prompt
"Simulate the transactional outbox pattern in-process. execute(topic, payload, business_fn) must apply the business mutation and append a Pending outbox row atomically (rollback both on business error — Vec + clone snapshot is fine). drain() publishes pending rows in order and marks them Published; second drain is empty."
Starter code to hand to candidate
enum OutboxStatus { Pending, Published }
struct OutboxRow { id: u64, topic: String, payload: String, status: OutboxStatus }

struct Outbox {
    rows: Vec<OutboxRow>,
    balances: std::collections::HashMap<String, i64>,
    // ...
}

impl Outbox {
    fn execute<F>(&mut self, topic: &str, payload: String, business_fn: F) -> Result<u64, String>
    where F: FnOnce(&mut HashMap<String, i64>) -> Result<(), String> { todo!() }
    fn drain(&mut self) -> Vec<(String, String)> { todo!() }
}


fn main() {
    let mut ob = Outbox::new();
    ob.execute("transfers", r#"{"to":"bob","amt":10}"#.into(), |bal| {
        let a = bal.entry("alice".into()).or_insert(100);
        if *a < 10 {
            return Err("insufficient".into());
        }
        *a -= 10;
        *bal.entry("bob".into()).or_insert(0) += 10;
        Ok(())
    })
    .unwrap();

    assert_eq!(ob.balances["alice"], 90);
    assert_eq!(ob.balances["bob"], 10);
    assert_eq!(ob.pending_count(), 1);

    // Failed business fn must not leave an outbox row
    let err = ob
        .execute("transfers", r#"{"to":"bob","amt":1000}"#.into(), |bal| {
            let a = bal.entry("alice".into()).or_insert(0);
            if *a < 1000 {
                return Err("insufficient".into());
            }
            Ok(())
        })
        .unwrap_err();
    assert_eq!(err, "insufficient");
    assert_eq!(ob.pending_count(), 1);
    assert_eq!(ob.balances["alice"], 90);

    ob.execute("transfers", r#"{"to":"carol","amt":5}"#.into(), |bal| {
        *bal.get_mut("alice").unwrap() -= 5;
        *bal.entry("carol".into()).or_insert(0) += 5;
        Ok(())
    })
    .unwrap();

    let pubbed = ob.drain();
    assert_eq!(pubbed.len(), 2);
    assert_eq!(pubbed[0].0, "transfers");
    assert!(pubbed[0].1.contains("bob"));
    assert!(pubbed[1].1.contains("carol"));
    assert_eq!(ob.pending_count(), 0);
    assert!(ob.drain().is_empty()); // idempotent drain

    println!("W88 ok");
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
enum OutboxStatus {
    Pending,
    Published,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
struct OutboxRow {
    id: u64,
    topic: String,
    payload: String,
    status: OutboxStatus,
}

struct Outbox {
    rows: Vec<OutboxRow>,
    next_id: u64,
    /// Simulated "business table"
    balances: std::collections::HashMap<String, i64>,
}

impl Outbox {
    fn new() -> Self {
        Self {
            rows: Vec::new(),
            next_id: 1,
            balances: std::collections::HashMap::new(),
        }
    }

    /// Atomically (simulated) run business mutation + append pending outbox row.
    fn execute<F>(&mut self, topic: &str, payload: String, business_fn: F) -> Result<u64, String>
    where
        F: FnOnce(&mut std::collections::HashMap<String, i64>) -> Result<(), String>,
    {
        // Snapshot for rollback on business error
        let snap_balances = self.balances.clone();
        let snap_rows_len = self.rows.len();
        let snap_next = self.next_id;

        if let Err(e) = business_fn(&mut self.balances) {
            self.balances = snap_balances;
            self.rows.truncate(snap_rows_len);
            self.next_id = snap_next;
            return Err(e);
        }

        let id = self.next_id;
        self.next_id += 1;
        self.rows.push(OutboxRow {
            id,
            topic: topic.to_string(),
            payload,
            status: OutboxStatus::Pending,
        });
        Ok(id)
    }

    /// Publish pending rows in insertion order; mark Published.
    fn drain(&mut self) -> Vec<(String, String)> {
        let mut published = Vec::new();
        for row in &mut self.rows {
            if row.status == OutboxStatus::Pending {
                published.push((row.topic.clone(), row.payload.clone()));
                row.status = OutboxStatus::Published;
            }
        }
        published
    }

    fn pending_count(&self) -> usize {
        self.rows
            .iter()
            .filter(|r| r.status == OutboxStatus::Pending)
            .count()
    }
}

fn main() {
    let mut ob = Outbox::new();
    ob.execute("transfers", r#"{"to":"bob","amt":10}"#.into(), |bal| {
        let a = bal.entry("alice".into()).or_insert(100);
        if *a < 10 {
            return Err("insufficient".into());
        }
        *a -= 10;
        *bal.entry("bob".into()).or_insert(0) += 10;
        Ok(())
    })
    .unwrap();

    assert_eq!(ob.balances["alice"], 90);
    assert_eq!(ob.balances["bob"], 10);
    assert_eq!(ob.pending_count(), 1);

    // Failed business fn must not leave an outbox row
    let err = ob
        .execute("transfers", r#"{"to":"bob","amt":1000}"#.into(), |bal| {
            let a = bal.entry("alice".into()).or_insert(0);
            if *a < 1000 {
                return Err("insufficient".into());
            }
            Ok(())
        })
        .unwrap_err();
    assert_eq!(err, "insufficient");
    assert_eq!(ob.pending_count(), 1);
    assert_eq!(ob.balances["alice"], 90);

    ob.execute("transfers", r#"{"to":"carol","amt":5}"#.into(), |bal| {
        *bal.get_mut("alice").unwrap() -= 5;
        *bal.entry("carol".into()).or_insert(0) += 5;
        Ok(())
    })
    .unwrap();

    let pubbed = ob.drain();
    assert_eq!(pubbed.len(), 2);
    assert_eq!(pubbed[0].0, "transfers");
    assert!(pubbed[0].1.contains("bob"));
    assert!(pubbed[1].1.contains("carol"));
    assert_eq!(ob.pending_count(), 0);
    assert!(ob.drain().is_empty()); // idempotent drain

    println!("W88 ok");
}
What to look for — unprompted signals
  • ★★★Atomicity simulation — failed business_fn rolls back balances AND does not leave a pending row.
  • ★★★drain is ordered and flips status so republish does not duplicate in this model.
  • ★★Separates business write from publish — the dual-write problem named explicitly.
  • ★Notes real impl uses DB transaction + poller / CDC (Debezium).
Follow-up probes
  • P1"At-least-once vs exactly-once to consumers?" — Outbox gives at-least-once publish; consumers still need idempotency keys.
  • P2"Why not emit to Kafka inside the DB transaction?" — Cannot atomically commit Kafka + SQL without outbox/CDC.
  • P3"Ordering guarantees?" — Per-aggregate ordering via partition key; global order is expensive.
🎯 Senior angle
The outbox exists because dual-writes lie. Senior candidates explain the failure mode (DB committed, message lost or vice versa) before writing code — then keep append+business in one atomic unit and publish asynchronously.

W89 · Length-Prefix Framed Codec
framing u32-be reassembly max-frame Medium
Prompt
"Implement a length-prefixed frame codec: wire format [u32 big-endian length][payload]. encode, decode_one (Incomplete / FrameTooLarge), and a streaming push(chunk) -> Vec<frame> that reassembles across partial reads. Reject frames above max_frame."
Starter code to hand to candidate
enum CodecError { FrameTooLarge { len: u32, max: u32 }, Incomplete }

struct FrameCodec { max_frame: u32, buf: Vec<u8> }

impl FrameCodec {
    fn new(max_frame: u32) -> Self { todo!() }
    fn encode(payload: &[u8]) -> Vec<u8> { todo!() }
    fn decode_one(data: &[u8], max_frame: u32) -> Result<(Vec<u8>, usize), CodecError> { todo!() }
    fn push(&mut self, chunk: &[u8]) -> Result<Vec<Vec<u8>>, CodecError> { todo!() }
}


fn main() {
    let f1 = FrameCodec::encode(b"hi");
    let f2 = FrameCodec::encode(b"world");
    assert_eq!(&f1[..4], &[0, 0, 0, 2]);
    let (p, n) = FrameCodec::decode_one(&f1, 1024).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(p, b"hi");
    assert_eq!(n, 6);

    assert_eq!(
        FrameCodec::decode_one(&[0, 0, 1, 0], 64),
        Err(CodecError::FrameTooLarge { len: 256, max: 64 })
    );
    assert_eq!(
        FrameCodec::decode_one(&[0, 0, 0, 5, 1, 2], 1024),
        Err(CodecError::Incomplete)

Full solution key — reveal after candidate finishes 
#[derive(Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
enum CodecError {
    FrameTooLarge { len: u32, max: u32 },
    Incomplete,
}

struct FrameCodec {
    max_frame: u32,
    buf: Vec<u8>,
}

impl FrameCodec {
    fn new(max_frame: u32) -> Self {
        Self {
            max_frame,
            buf: Vec::new(),
        }
    }

    fn encode(payload: &[u8]) -> Vec<u8> {
        let mut out = Vec::with_capacity(4 + payload.len());
        out.extend_from_slice(&(payload.len() as u32).to_be_bytes());
        out.extend_from_slice(payload);
        out
    }

    fn decode_one(data: &[u8], max_frame: u32) -> Result<(Vec<u8>, usize), CodecError> {
        if data.len() < 4 {
            return Err(CodecError::Incomplete);
        }
        let len = u32::from_be_bytes(data[0..4].try_into().unwrap());
        if len > max_frame {
            return Err(CodecError::FrameTooLarge {
                len,
                max: max_frame,
            });
        }
        let total = 4 + len as usize;
        if data.len() < total {
            return Err(CodecError::Incomplete);
        }
        Ok((data[4..total].to_vec(), total))
    }

    /// Push bytes; return zero or more complete frames.
    fn push(&mut self, chunk: &[u8]) -> Result<Vec<Vec<u8>>, CodecError> {
        self.buf.extend_from_slice(chunk);
        let mut frames = Vec::new();
        loop {
            match Self::decode_one(&self.buf, self.max_frame) {
                Ok((payload, consumed)) => {
                    self.buf.drain(..consumed);
                    frames.push(payload);
                }
                Err(CodecError::Incomplete) => break,
                Err(e) => return Err(e),
            }
        }
        Ok(frames)
    }
}

fn main() {
    let f1 = FrameCodec::encode(b"hi");
    let f2 = FrameCodec::encode(b"world");
    assert_eq!(&f1[..4], &[0, 0, 0, 2]);
    let (p, n) = FrameCodec::decode_one(&f1, 1024).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(p, b"hi");
    assert_eq!(n, 6);

    assert_eq!(
        FrameCodec::decode_one(&[0, 0, 1, 0], 64),
        Err(CodecError::FrameTooLarge { len: 256, max: 64 })
    );
    assert_eq!(
        FrameCodec::decode_one(&[0, 0, 0, 5, 1, 2], 1024),
        Err(CodecError::Incomplete)
    );

    let mut codec = FrameCodec::new(1024);
    let mut stream = Vec::new();
    stream.extend_from_slice(&f1);
    stream.extend_from_slice(&f2);

    // Feed one byte at a time — reassembly must work
    let mut got = Vec::new();
    for byte in &stream {
        got.extend(codec.push(&[*byte]).unwrap());
    }
    assert_eq!(got, vec![b"hi".to_vec(), b"world".to_vec()]);
    assert!(codec.buf.is_empty());

    println!("W89 ok");
}
What to look for — unprompted signals
  • ★★★Streaming reassembly buffer — handles 1-byte chunks without losing sync.
  • ★★★Max frame size enforced before allocating payload — DoS guard.
  • ★★Big-endian length (network byte order) called out.
  • ★Returns consumed byte count so callers can advance a cursor.
Follow-up probes
  • P1"LE vs BE?" — On the wire, BE is conventional; pick one and document it.
  • P2"What if length lies?" — Cap max_frame; optionally add checksums (see WAL exercise).
  • P3"Zero-copy?" — Decode into Bytes/cursor slices; avoid to_vec per frame on hot paths.
🎯 Senior angle
Framing bugs are security bugs. Seniors bound frame size before allocation, keep an explicit read buffer, and never assume TCP delivers one message per read.

Full solution key — reveal after candidate finishes 
use std::collections::VecDeque;

struct SlidingWindow {
    limit: usize,
    window_ms: u64,
    events: VecDeque<u64>,
}

impl SlidingWindow {
    fn new(limit: usize, window_ms: u64) -> Self {
        Self {
            limit,
            window_ms,
            events: VecDeque::new(),
        }
    }

    fn allow(&mut self, now_ms: u64) -> bool {
        let cutoff = now_ms.saturating_sub(self.window_ms);
        while self.events.front().is_some_and(|&t| t <= cutoff) {
            self.events.pop_front();
        }
        if self.events.len() < self.limit {
            self.events.push_back(now_ms);
            true
        } else {
            false
        }
    }
}

/// Leaky bucket: capacity (burst) + leak_rate per ms (as fixed-point: leak_per_1000ms).
struct LeakyBucket {
    capacity: f64,
    leak_per_ms: f64,
    level: f64,
    last_ms: u64,
}

impl LeakyBucket {
    fn new(capacity: f64, leak_per_sec: f64) -> Self {
        Self {
            capacity,
            leak_per_ms: leak_per_sec / 1000.0,
            level: 0.0,
            last_ms: 0,
        }
    }

    fn allow(&mut self, now_ms: u64) -> bool {
        if now_ms > self.last_ms {
            let leaked = (now_ms - self.last_ms) as f64 * self.leak_per_ms;
            self.level = (self.level - leaked).max(0.0);
            self.last_ms = now_ms;
        }
        if self.level + 1.0 <= self.capacity {
            self.level += 1.0;
            true
        } else {
            false
        }
    }
}

fn main() {
    let mut sw = SlidingWindow::new(3, 1000);
    assert!(sw.allow(100));
    assert!(sw.allow(200));
    assert!(sw.allow(300));
    assert!(!sw.allow(400)); // 4th inside window
    assert!(sw.allow(1101)); // oldest (100) fell out of [101, 1101]

    let mut lb = LeakyBucket::new(2.0, 1.0); // capacity 2, leak 1/sec
    assert!(lb.allow(0));
    assert!(lb.allow(0));
    assert!(!lb.allow(0)); // burst exhausted
    assert!(lb.allow(1000)); // one token leaked

    println!("W90 ok");
}
What to look for — unprompted signals
  • ★★★Evicts timestamps outside the window before counting — true sliding window, not fixed buckets.
  • ★★Implements both algorithms and can explain burst vs smooth leak.
  • ★★Injected clock — no Instant::now in the limiter core.
  • ★Mentions distributed limiters need Redis/atomic stores.
Follow-up probes
  • P1"Sliding window vs token bucket vs fixed window?" — Fixed window has boundary burst; sliding is fairer; token/leaky control sustained rate + burst.
  • P2"Memory for sliding window?" — O(N) timestamps; approximate with sliding log or window counters.
  • P3"f64 for leaky level?" — Fine for interview; production often uses integer micros to avoid drift.
🎯 Senior angle
Rate limiting is an API-design + clock-discipline problem. Strong candidates pick a clear algorithm, inject time, and can explain which burst patterns each limiter permits.

"Implement bucket(user_id, flag_salt) -> 0..99 using a stable hash, plus in_rollout(user, salt, percent). Rollouts must be sticky: raising percent from 10→20 keeps everyone who was already enabled. Prove stability with unit tests (same inputs ⇒ same bucket; roughly uniform distribution)."

fn bucket(user_id: &str, flag_salt: &str) -> u8 { todo!("0..99") }
fn in_rollout(user_id: &str, flag_salt: &str, percent: u8) -> bool { todo!() }


fn main() {
    // Stability: same inputs always same bucket
    let b = bucket("user-42", "new-checkout");
    for _ in 0..50 {
        assert_eq!(bucket("user-42", "new-checkout"), b);
    }
    assert!(b < 100);

    // Sticky percentage: 0% nobody, 100% everybody
    assert!(!in_rollout("anyone", "x", 0));
    assert!(in_rollout("anyone", "x", 100));

    // Distribution roughly uniform across many users
    let mut counts = [0u32; 100];
    for i in 0..10_000 {
        counts[bucket(&format!("u{i}"), "rollout") as usize] += 1;
    }
    let min = *counts.iter().min().unwrap();

    assert!(min > 50 && max < 200, "min={min} max={max}");

    let mut enabled_at_10 = Vec::new();
    for i in 0..1000 {

fn fnv1a64(bytes: &[u8]) -> u64 {
    let mut h: u64 = 0xcbf29ce484222325;
    for &b in bytes {
        h ^= b as u64;
        h = h.wrapping_mul(0x100000001b3);
    }
    h
}

/// Stable bucket in 0..99 for sticky percentage rollouts.
fn bucket(user_id: &str, flag_salt: &str) -> u8 {
    let mut data = Vec::with_capacity(user_id.len() + 1 + flag_salt.len());
    data.extend_from_slice(user_id.as_bytes());
    data.push(0xff);
    data.extend_from_slice(flag_salt.as_bytes());
    (fnv1a64(&data) % 100) as u8
}

fn in_rollout(user_id: &str, flag_salt: &str, percent: u8) -> bool {
    assert!(percent <= 100);
    bucket(user_id, flag_salt) < percent
}

fn main() {
    // Stability: same inputs always same bucket
    let b = bucket("user-42", "new-checkout");
    for _ in 0..50 {
        assert_eq!(bucket("user-42", "new-checkout"), b);
    }
    assert!(b < 100);

    // Sticky percentage: 0% nobody, 100% everybody
    assert!(!in_rollout("anyone", "x", 0));
    assert!(in_rollout("anyone", "x", 100));

    // Distribution roughly uniform across many users
    let mut counts = [0u32; 100];
    for i in 0..10_000 {
        counts[bucket(&format!("u{i}"), "rollout") as usize] += 1;
    }
    let min = *counts.iter().min().unwrap();
    let max = *counts.iter().max().unwrap();
    assert!(min > 50 && max < 200, "min={min} max={max}");

    // Sticky: raising percent from 10→20 keeps all previously-enabled users
    let mut enabled_at_10 = Vec::new();
    for i in 0..1000 {
        let u = format!("user{i}");
        if in_rollout(&u, "sticky", 10) {
            enabled_at_10.push(u);
        }
    }
    assert!(!enabled_at_10.is_empty());
    for u in &enabled_at_10 {
        assert!(in_rollout(u, "sticky", 20));
    }

    println!("W91 ok bucket(user-42)={b}");
}

// ── Compact SHA-256 (FIPS 180-4) ──────────────────────────────────────────
fn sha256(msg: &[u8]) -> [u8; 32] {
    const K: [u32; 64] = [
        0x428a2f98, 0x71374491, 0xb5c0fbcf, 0xe9b5dba5, 0x3956c25b, 0x59f111f1, 0x923f82a4,
        0xab1c5ed5, 0xd807aa98, 0x12835b01, 0x243185be, 0x550c7dc3, 0x72be5d74, 0x80deb1fe,
        0x9bdc06a7, 0xc19bf174, 0xe49b69c1, 0xefbe4786, 0x0fc19dc6, 0x240ca1cc, 0x2de92c6f,
        0x4a7484aa, 0x5cb0a9dc, 0x76f988da, 0x983e5152, 0xa831c66d, 0xb00327c8, 0xbf597fc7,
        0xc6e00bf3, 0xd5a79147, 0x06ca6351, 0x14292967, 0x27b70a85, 0x2e1b2138, 0x4d2c6dfc,
        0x53380d13, 0x650a7354, 0x766a0abb, 0x81c2c92e, 0x92722c85, 0xa2bfe8a1, 0xa81a664b,
        0xc24b8b70, 0xc76c51a3, 0xd192e819, 0xd6990624, 0xf40e3585, 0x106aa070, 0x19a4c116,
        0x1e376c08, 0x2748774c, 0x34b0bcb5, 0x391c0cb3, 0x4ed8aa4a, 0x5b9cca4f, 0x682e6ff3,
        0x748f82ee, 0x78a5636f, 0x84c87814, 0x8cc70208, 0x90befffa, 0xa4506ceb, 0xbef9a3f7,
        0xc67178f2,
    ];
    let mut h: [u32; 8] = [
        0x6a09e667, 0xbb67ae85, 0x3c6ef372, 0xa54ff53a, 0x510e527f, 0x9b05688c, 0x1f83d9ab,
        0x5be0cd19,
    ];
    let bit_len = (msg.len() as u64) * 8;
    let mut data = msg.to_vec();
    data.push(0x80);
    while (data.len() % 64) != 56 {
        data.push(0);
    }
    data.extend_from_slice(&bit_len.to_be_bytes());

    for chunk in data.chunks_exact(64) {
        let mut w = [0u32; 64];
        for i in 0..16 {
            w[i] = u32::from_be_bytes(chunk[i * 4..i * 4 + 4].try_into().unwrap());
        }
        for i in 16..64 {
            let s0 = w[i - 15].rotate_right(7) ^ w[i - 15].rotate_right(18) ^ (w[i - 15] >> 3);
            let s1 = w[i - 2].rotate_right(17) ^ w[i - 2].rotate_right(19) ^ (w[i - 2] >> 10);
            w[i] = w[i - 16]
                .wrapping_add(s0)
                .wrapping_add(w[i - 7])
                .wrapping_add(s1);
        }
        let mut a = h[0];
        let mut b = h[1];
        let mut c = h[2];
        let mut d = h[3];
        let mut e = h[4];
        let mut f = h[5];
        let mut g = h[6];
        let mut hh = h[7];
        for i in 0..64 {
            let s1 = e.rotate_right(6) ^ e.rotate_right(11) ^ e.rotate_right(25);
            let ch = (e & f) ^ ((!e) & g);
            let t1 = hh
                .wrapping_add(s1)
                .wrapping_add(ch)
                .wrapping_add(K[i])
                .wrapping_add(w[i]);
            let s0 = a.rotate_right(2) ^ a.rotate_right(13) ^ a.rotate_right(22);
            let maj = (a & b) ^ (a & c) ^ (b & c);
            let t2 = s0.wrapping_add(maj);
            hh = g;
            g = f;
            f = e;
            e = d.wrapping_add(t1);
            d = c;
            c = b;
            b = a;
            a = t1.wrapping_add(t2);
        }
        h[0] = h[0].wrapping_add(a);
        h[1] = h[1].wrapping_add(b);
        h[2] = h[2].wrapping_add(c);
        h[3] = h[3].wrapping_add(d);
        h[4] = h[4].wrapping_add(e);
        h[5] = h[5].wrapping_add(f);
        h[6] = h[6].wrapping_add(g);
        h[7] = h[7].wrapping_add(hh);
    }
    let mut out = [0u8; 32];
    for (i, v) in h.iter().enumerate() {
        out[i * 4..i * 4 + 4].copy_from_slice(&v.to_be_bytes());
    }
    out
}

fn hmac_sha256(key: &[u8], msg: &[u8]) -> [u8; 32] {
    const BLOCK: usize = 64;
    let mut k = if key.len() > BLOCK {
        sha256(key).to_vec()
    } else {
        key.to_vec()
    };
    k.resize(BLOCK, 0);
    let mut ipad = [0x36u8; BLOCK];
    let mut opad = [0x5cu8; BLOCK];
    for i in 0..BLOCK {
        ipad[i] ^= k[i];
        opad[i] ^= k[i];
    }
    let mut inner = Vec::with_capacity(BLOCK + msg.len());
    inner.extend_from_slice(&ipad);
    inner.extend_from_slice(msg);
    let inner_hash = sha256(&inner);
    let mut outer = Vec::with_capacity(BLOCK + 32);
    outer.extend_from_slice(&opad);
    outer.extend_from_slice(&inner_hash);
    sha256(&outer)
}

fn to_hex(bytes: &[u8]) -> String {
    bytes.iter().map(|b| format!("{b:02x}")).collect()
}

fn verify_signature(secret: &[u8], body: &[u8], header: &str) -> bool {
    // header format: "sha256=<hex>"
    let Some(hex) = header.strip_prefix("sha256=") else {
        return false;
    };
    let expected = to_hex(&hmac_sha256(secret, body));
    // Constant-time-ish compare for interview purposes
    if expected.len() != hex.len() {
        return false;
    }
    expected
        .bytes()
        .zip(hex.bytes())
        .fold(0u8, |acc, (a, b)| acc | (a ^ b))
        == 0
}

/// Deterministic exponential backoff with bounded jitter from seed.
fn backoff_ms(attempt: u32, base_ms: u64, max_ms: u64, seed: u64) -> u64 {
    let exp = base_ms.saturating_mul(1u64 << attempt.min(20));
    let capped = exp.min(max_ms);
    // jitter in [0, capped/4]
    let jitter_span = capped / 4;
    let jitter = if jitter_span == 0 {
        0
    } else {
        (seed.wrapping_mul(6364136223846793005).wrapping_add(attempt as u64)) % (jitter_span + 1)
    };
    (capped / 2).saturating_add(jitter).min(max_ms)
}

fn main() {
    // RFC 4231 test case 1
    let mac = hmac_sha256(b"key", b"The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog");
    assert_eq!(
        to_hex(&mac),
        "f7bc83f430538424b13298e6aa6fb143ef4d59a14946175997479dbc2d1a3cd8"
    );

    let secret = b"whsec_test";
    let body = br#"{"id":1}"#;
    let sig = format!("sha256={}", to_hex(&hmac_sha256(secret, body)));
    assert!(verify_signature(secret, body, &sig));
    assert!(!verify_signature(secret, body, "sha256=deadbeef"));
    assert!(!verify_signature(secret, b"tampered", &sig));

    let d0 = backoff_ms(0, 100, 10_000, 42);
    let d3 = backoff_ms(3, 100, 10_000, 42);
    let d10 = backoff_ms(10, 100, 10_000, 42);
    assert!(d0 >= 50 && d0 <= 100);
    assert!(d3 > d0);
    assert!(d10 <= 10_000 && d10 >= 5_000); // exp capped at max; jitter keeps it in [max/2, max]
    // Deterministic for same seed
    assert_eq!(backoff_ms(2, 100, 10_000, 7), backoff_ms(2, 100, 10_000, 7));

    println!("W92 ok");
}
What to look for — unprompted signals
  • ★★★Real HMAC construction (ipad/opad) over SHA-256 — not just hash(key||msg) unless explicitly stubbed.
  • ★★Rejects tampered body / bad header; compares digests without early-exit string equality if they mention it.
  • ★★Backoff caps at max_delay and jitter is bounded (no unbounded sleep).
  • ★Knows to use a secret from env/KMS and rotate signing keys.
Follow-up probes
  • P1"Replay attacks?" — Include timestamp/nonce in signed payload; reject stale timestamps.
  • P2"Why jitter?" — Avoid thundering herds when many webhooks fail together.
  • P3"Constant-time compare?" — Prevents timing leaks on the hex digest; std has subtle crates / manual XOR fold.
🎯 Senior angle
Webhook security is HMAC + replay protection + careful retries. Implementing SHA-256 from the spec under time pressure is a strong systems signal; falling back to a documented stub is acceptable if they still get the HMAC outer structure right.

Full solution key — reveal after candidate finishes 
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
struct Cursor {
    sort_key: i64,
    id: u64,
}

#[derive(Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
enum CursorError {
    InvalidEncoding,
    BadVersion,
}

impl Cursor {
    fn encode(&self) -> String {
        // version byte + sort_key + id, then base64url-ish (hex for std-only simplicity)
        let mut raw = Vec::with_capacity(1 + 8 + 8);
        raw.push(1u8); // version
        raw.extend_from_slice(&self.sort_key.to_be_bytes());
        raw.extend_from_slice(&self.id.to_be_bytes());
        // hex encode (opaque to clients)
        raw.iter().map(|b| format!("{b:02x}")).collect()
    }

    fn decode(s: &str) -> Result<Self, CursorError> {
        if s.len() != 34 || !s.chars().all(|c| c.is_ascii_hexdigit()) {
            return Err(CursorError::InvalidEncoding);
        }
        let mut raw = [0u8; 17];
        for i in 0..17 {
            raw[i] = u8::from_str_radix(&s[i * 2..i * 2 + 2], 16)
                .map_err(|_| CursorError::InvalidEncoding)?;
        }
        if raw[0] != 1 {
            return Err(CursorError::BadVersion);
        }
        let sort_key = i64::from_be_bytes(raw[1..9].try_into().unwrap());
        let id = u64::from_be_bytes(raw[9..17].try_into().unwrap());
        Ok(Self { sort_key, id })
    }
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
struct Row {
    sort_key: i64,
    id: u64,
    name: String,
}

struct Page {
    items: Vec<Row>,
    next_cursor: Option<String>,
}

fn paginate(rows: &[Row], after: Option<&str>, limit: usize) -> Result<Page, CursorError> {
    assert!(limit > 0);
    let start = if let Some(c) = after {
        let cur = Cursor::decode(c)?;
        rows.iter()
            .position(|r| {
                (r.sort_key, r.id) > (cur.sort_key, cur.id)
            })
            .unwrap_or(rows.len())
    } else {
        0
    };
    let end = (start + limit).min(rows.len());
    let items = rows[start..end].to_vec();
    let next_cursor = if end < rows.len() {
        let last = items.last().unwrap();
        Some(
            Cursor {
                sort_key: last.sort_key,
                id: last.id,
            }
            .encode(),
        )
    } else {
        None
    };
    Ok(Page { items, next_cursor })
}

fn main() {
    let rows = vec![
        Row { sort_key: 10, id: 1, name: "a".into() },
        Row { sort_key: 10, id: 2, name: "b".into() },
        Row { sort_key: 20, id: 3, name: "c".into() },
        Row { sort_key: 30, id: 4, name: "d".into() },
        Row { sort_key: 30, id: 5, name: "e".into() },
    ];

    let p1 = paginate(&rows, None, 2).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(p1.items.len(), 2);
    assert_eq!(p1.items[0].name, "a");
    assert!(p1.next_cursor.is_some());

    let p2 = paginate(&rows, p1.next_cursor.as_deref(), 2).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(p2.items.iter().map(|r| r.name.as_str()).collect::<Vec<_>>(), vec!["c", "d"]);

    let p3 = paginate(&rows, p2.next_cursor.as_deref(), 2).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(p3.items.len(), 1);
    assert_eq!(p3.items[0].name, "e");
    assert!(p3.next_cursor.is_none());

    // Round-trip encode/decode
    let c = Cursor { sort_key: -5, id: 99 };
    assert_eq!(Cursor::decode(&c.encode()).unwrap(), c);
    assert_eq!(Cursor::decode("zz"), Err(CursorError::InvalidEncoding));

    // Tie-break on id when sort_key equal
    let after_a = Cursor { sort_key: 10, id: 1 }.encode();
    let page = paginate(&rows, Some(&after_a), 1).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(page.items[0].id, 2);

    println!("W93 ok");
}
What to look for — unprompted signals
  • ★★★Seek by (sort_key, id) — not OFFSET — and tie-breaks correctly.
  • ★★Opaque versioned encoding with validation on decode.
  • ★★next_cursor is None on the last page — clear API contract.
  • ★Mentions signed/encrypted cursors in production to prevent tampering.
Follow-up probes
  • P1"Why not OFFSET/LIMIT?" — Skips/duplicates under concurrent inserts; cost grows with offset.
  • P2"Descending order?" — Encode direction or negate keys; keep comparison consistent.
  • P3"Unstable sort columns?" — Always include a unique tie-breaker (primary key).
🎯 Senior angle
Cursor pagination is seek-method indexing in disguise. Seniors always include a unique tie-breaker and treat cursors as potentially hostile input (version + validate, optionally MAC).

Full solution key — reveal after candidate finishes 
/// Price in ticks, qty in lots. Notional accumulates as i128 to avoid overflow.
struct Vwap {
    notional: i128, // sum(price * qty)
    qty: i64,
}

impl Vwap {
    fn new() -> Self {
        Self { notional: 0, qty: 0 }
    }

    fn on_trade(&mut self, price_ticks: i64, qty: i64) {
        assert!(qty > 0 && price_ticks > 0);
        self.notional += price_ticks as i128 * qty as i128;
        self.qty += qty;
    }

    /// Floor VWAP in ticks; None if no trades.
    fn vwap_ticks(&self) -> Option<i64> {
        if self.qty == 0 {
            None
        } else {
            Some((self.notional / self.qty as i128) as i64)
        }
    }
}

fn main() {
    let mut v = Vwap::new();
    assert_eq!(v.vwap_ticks(), None);

    v.on_trade(100, 10); // 1000
    assert_eq!(v.vwap_ticks(), Some(100));

    v.on_trade(110, 10); // +1100 → notional 2100 / 20 = 105
    assert_eq!(v.vwap_ticks(), Some(105));

    v.on_trade(90, 20); // +1800 → 3900 / 40 = 97
    assert_eq!(v.vwap_ticks(), Some(97));

    // Large numbers stay in i128
    let mut big = Vwap::new();
    big.on_trade(1_000_000_000, 1_000_000);
    big.on_trade(2_000_000_000, 1_000_000);
    assert_eq!(big.vwap_ticks(), Some(1_500_000_000));

    println!("W94 ok");
}

Full solution key — reveal after candidate finishes 
use std::collections::HashMap;

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
struct Quote {
    price: i64,
    qty: i64,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
struct Bbo {
    bid: Option<Quote>,
    ask: Option<Quote>,
}

struct VenueBook {
    bid: Option<Quote>,
    ask: Option<Quote>,
}

struct BboAggregator {
    venues: HashMap<String, VenueBook>,
}

impl BboAggregator {
    fn new() -> Self {
        Self {
            venues: HashMap::new(),
        }
    }

    fn update_venue(&mut self, venue: &str, bid: Option<Quote>, ask: Option<Quote>) {
        self.venues.insert(
            venue.to_string(),
            VenueBook { bid, ask },
        );
    }

    fn remove_venue(&mut self, venue: &str) {
        self.venues.remove(venue);
    }

    fn aggregated(&self) -> Bbo {
        let mut best_bid: Option<Quote> = None;
        let mut best_ask: Option<Quote> = None;
        for book in self.venues.values() {
            if let Some(b) = book.bid {
                best_bid = Some(match best_bid {
                    None => b,
                    Some(cur) if b.price > cur.price => b,
                    Some(cur) if b.price == cur.price && b.qty > cur.qty => b,
                    Some(cur) => cur,
                });
            }
            if let Some(a) = book.ask {
                best_ask = Some(match best_ask {
                    None => a,
                    Some(cur) if a.price < cur.price => a,
                    Some(cur) if a.price == cur.price && a.qty > cur.qty => a,
                    Some(cur) => cur,
                });
            }
        }
        Bbo {
            bid: best_bid,
            ask: best_ask,
        }
    }
}

fn main() {
    let mut agg = BboAggregator::new();
    assert_eq!(agg.aggregated(), Bbo { bid: None, ask: None });

    agg.update_venue(
        "NYSE",
        Some(Quote { price: 100, qty: 5 }),
        Some(Quote { price: 102, qty: 3 }),
    );
    agg.update_venue(
        "ARCA",
        Some(Quote { price: 101, qty: 2 }),
        Some(Quote { price: 103, qty: 4 }),
    );
    let bbo = agg.aggregated();
    assert_eq!(bbo.bid, Some(Quote { price: 101, qty: 2 })); // ARCA better bid
    assert_eq!(bbo.ask, Some(Quote { price: 102, qty: 3 })); // NYSE better ask

    // Empty side on one venue is fine
    agg.update_venue("BATS", Some(Quote { price: 99, qty: 10 }), None);
    assert_eq!(agg.aggregated().ask, Some(Quote { price: 102, qty: 3 }));

    // Venue with only ask
    agg.update_venue("DARK", None, Some(Quote { price: 101, qty: 1 }));
    assert_eq!(agg.aggregated().ask, Some(Quote { price: 101, qty: 1 }));

    agg.remove_venue("DARK");
    assert_eq!(agg.aggregated().ask, Some(Quote { price: 102, qty: 3 }));

    println!("W95 ok");
}
What to look for — unprompted signals
  • ★★★Handles empty sides without inventing 0 prices.
  • ★★★Correct best bid (max) / best ask (min) across venues.
  • ★★Remove/update venue recomputes cleanly.
  • ★Mentions locked/crossed markets as a data-quality check.
Follow-up probes
  • P1"NBBO vs synthetic BBO?" — Regulated NBBO has SIP rules; internal aggregator may differ.
  • P2"Stale venue quotes?" — Heartbeats / sequence / TTL per venue before including in BBO.
  • P3"Allocation on hot path?" — Fixed venue slots beat HashMap String keys in latency shops.

Full solution key — reveal after candidate finishes 
#[derive(Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
struct Request {
    method: String,
    path: String,
    version: String,
    headers: Vec<(String, String)>,
}

#[derive(Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
enum ParseError {
    Incomplete,
    BadRequestLine,
    TooManyHeaders,
    HeaderTooLarge,
    InvalidHeader,
    SmugglingRisk,
}

const MAX_HEADERS: usize = 32;
const MAX_HEADER_SIZE: usize = 256;

fn parse_request(raw: &str) -> Result<Request, ParseError> {
    let (head, _rest) = raw.split_once("\r\n\r\n").ok_or(ParseError::Incomplete)?;
    let mut lines = head.split("\r\n");
    let req_line = lines.next().ok_or(ParseError::BadRequestLine)?;
    let mut parts = req_line.split(' ');
    let method = parts.next().ok_or(ParseError::BadRequestLine)?.to_string();
    let path = parts.next().ok_or(ParseError::BadRequestLine)?.to_string();
    let version = parts.next().ok_or(ParseError::BadRequestLine)?.to_string();
    if parts.next().is_some() || !version.starts_with("HTTP/") {
        return Err(ParseError::BadRequestLine);
    }
    if method.is_empty() || path.is_empty() || method.bytes().any(|b| b == b'\t' || b == b'\n') {
        return Err(ParseError::BadRequestLine);
    }

    let mut headers = Vec::new();
    for line in lines {
        if headers.len() >= MAX_HEADERS {
            return Err(ParseError::TooManyHeaders);
        }
        if line.len() > MAX_HEADER_SIZE {
            return Err(ParseError::HeaderTooLarge);
        }
        // Reject bare essentials of smuggling: embedded CR/LF already split; reject space before colon,
        // empty names, Transfer-Encoding + Content-Length together.
        if line.starts_with(' ') || line.starts_with('\t') {
            return Err(ParseError::InvalidHeader); // obs-fold / smuggling-ish
        }
        let (name, value) = line.split_once(':').ok_or(ParseError::InvalidHeader)?;
        if name.is_empty() || name.bytes().any(|b| b == b' ' || b == b'\t') {
            return Err(ParseError::InvalidHeader);
        }
        headers.push((name.to_ascii_lowercase(), value.trim().to_string()));
    }

    let has_cl = headers.iter().any(|(n, _)| n == "content-length");
    let has_te = headers.iter().any(|(n, _)| n == "transfer-encoding");
    if has_cl && has_te {
        return Err(ParseError::SmugglingRisk);
    }
    // Duplicate Content-Length
    if headers.iter().filter(|(n, _)| n == "content-length").count() > 1 {
        return Err(ParseError::SmugglingRisk);
    }

    Ok(Request {
        method,
        path,
        version,
        headers,
    })
}

fn main() {
    let ok = "GET /hi HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: example.com\r\nUser-Agent: test\r\n\r\n";
    let r = parse_request(ok).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(r.method, "GET");
    assert_eq!(r.path, "/hi");
    assert_eq!(r.headers.len(), 2);
    assert_eq!(r.headers[0].0, "host");

    assert_eq!(parse_request("GET / HTTP/1.1\r\n"), Err(ParseError::Incomplete));
    assert_eq!(
        parse_request("GET / HTTP/1.1\r\nContent-Length: 1\r\nTransfer-Encoding: chunked\r\n\r\n"),
        Err(ParseError::SmugglingRisk)
    );
    assert_eq!(
        parse_request("GET / HTTP/1.1\r\nBad Name: x\r\n\r\n"),
        Err(ParseError::InvalidHeader)
    );
    // folded header line
    assert_eq!(
        parse_request("GET / HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: a\r\n continued\r\n\r\n"),
        Err(ParseError::InvalidHeader)
    );

    let mut many = String::from("GET / HTTP/1.1\r\n");
    for i in 0..33 {
        many.push_str(&format!("X-{i}: v\r\n"));
    }
    many.push_str("\r\n");
    assert_eq!(parse_request(&many), Err(ParseError::TooManyHeaders));

    println!("W96 ok");
}
What to look for — unprompted signals
  • ★★★Rejects CL+TE and duplicate CL — names request smuggling.
  • ★★★Enforces header count/size limits (DoS).
  • ★★Requires \r\n\r\n terminator; Incomplete otherwise.
  • ★Normalizes header names to lowercase for comparison.
Follow-up probes
  • P1"Why is CL+TE dangerous?" — Front-end and back-end may disagree on framing → smuggling/cache poison.
  • P2"httparse vs hand-rolled?" — Production uses battle-tested parsers; interview tests threat model.
  • P3"Body parsing?" — Separate from headers; length from CL or chunked TE — never both.

HTTP parsing interviews are security interviews. Limits + smuggling rejects matter more than supporting every obsolete fold.

    fn new(strategy: Strategy) -> Self { todo!() }
