fn main() {
    let mut rr = LoadBalancer::new(Strategy::RoundRobin);
    rr.add_backend("a");
    rr.add_backend("b");
    rr.add_backend("c");
    assert_eq!(rr.pick_backend(), Some("a"));
    assert_eq!(rr.pick_backend(), Some("b"));
    assert_eq!(rr.pick_backend(), Some("c"));
    assert_eq!(rr.pick_backend(), Some("a"));
    rr.set_active("b", false);
    // Continues round-robin over remaining active set {a,c}
    let mut seen = vec![
        rr.pick_backend().unwrap().to_string(),
        rr.pick_backend().unwrap().to_string(),
        rr.pick_backend().unwrap().to_string(),
        rr.pick_backend().unwrap().to_string(),
    ];
    seen.sort();
    assert_eq!(seen, vec!["a", "a", "c", "c"]);

    let mut lc = LoadBalancer::new(Strategy::LeastConnections);
    lc.add_backend("x");
    lc.add_backend("y");
    assert_eq!(lc.pick_backend(), Some("x")); // ties break by index
    assert_eq!(lc.pick_backend(), Some("y"));
    assert_eq!(lc.pick_backend(), Some("x"));
    lc.release("x");
    lc.release("x");
    // x has 1, y has 1 after third pick... after two releases of x: x=0? 
    // picks: x(1), y(1), x(2); release x → 1; release x → 0. y still 1.
    assert_eq!(lc.backends[0].connections, 0);
    assert_eq!(lc.backends[1].connections, 1);
    assert_eq!(lc.pick_backend(), Some("x"));

    let mut empty = LoadBalancer::new(Strategy::RoundRobin);
    assert_eq!(empty.pick_backend(), None);

    println!("W97 ok");
}
Full solution key — reveal after candidate finishes 
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
struct Backend {
    id: String,
    active: bool,
    connections: u32,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
enum Strategy {
    RoundRobin,
    LeastConnections,
}

struct LoadBalancer {
    backends: Vec<Backend>,
    strategy: Strategy,
    rr_idx: usize,
}

impl LoadBalancer {
    fn new(strategy: Strategy) -> Self {
        Self {
            backends: Vec::new(),
            strategy,
            rr_idx: 0,
        }
    }

    fn add_backend(&mut self, id: &str) {
        self.backends.push(Backend {
            id: id.to_string(),
            active: true,
            connections: 0,
        });
    }

    fn set_active(&mut self, id: &str, active: bool) {
        if let Some(b) = self.backends.iter_mut().find(|b| b.id == id) {
            b.active = active;
        }
    }

    fn pick_backend(&mut self) -> Option<&str> {
        let active_idx: Vec<usize> = self
            .backends
            .iter()
            .enumerate()
            .filter(|(_, b)| b.active)
            .map(|(i, _)| i)
            .collect();
        if active_idx.is_empty() {
            return None;
        }
        let chosen = match self.strategy {
            Strategy::RoundRobin => {
                let i = active_idx[self.rr_idx % active_idx.len()];
                self.rr_idx = self.rr_idx.wrapping_add(1);
                i
            }
            Strategy::LeastConnections => *active_idx
                .iter()
                .min_by_key(|&&i| (self.backends[i].connections, i))
                .unwrap(),
        };
        self.backends[chosen].connections += 1;
        Some(self.backends[chosen].id.as_str())
    }

    fn release(&mut self, id: &str) {
        if let Some(b) = self.backends.iter_mut().find(|b| b.id == id) {
            b.connections = b.connections.saturating_sub(1);
        }
    }
}

fn main() {
    let mut rr = LoadBalancer::new(Strategy::RoundRobin);
    rr.add_backend("a");
    rr.add_backend("b");
    rr.add_backend("c");
    assert_eq!(rr.pick_backend(), Some("a"));
    assert_eq!(rr.pick_backend(), Some("b"));
    assert_eq!(rr.pick_backend(), Some("c"));
    assert_eq!(rr.pick_backend(), Some("a"));
    rr.set_active("b", false);
    // Continues round-robin over remaining active set {a,c}
    let mut seen = vec![
        rr.pick_backend().unwrap().to_string(),
        rr.pick_backend().unwrap().to_string(),
        rr.pick_backend().unwrap().to_string(),
        rr.pick_backend().unwrap().to_string(),
    ];
    seen.sort();
    assert_eq!(seen, vec!["a", "a", "c", "c"]);

    let mut lc = LoadBalancer::new(Strategy::LeastConnections);
    lc.add_backend("x");
    lc.add_backend("y");

"Implement RetryPolicy { max_attempts, base_delay, max_delay, budget } with next_delay(attempt) (exponential, capped). execute(op) classifies errors as retryable (Timeout/Unavailable) vs Fatal (no retry), and stops when the delay budget would be exceeded."
Starter code to hand to candidate
struct RetryPolicy {
    max_attempts: u32,
    base_delay_ms: u64,
    max_delay_ms: u64,
    budget_ms: u64,
}
enum CallError { Timeout, Unavailable, Fatal }

impl RetryPolicy {
    fn next_delay(&self, attempt: u32) -> Option<u64> { todo!() }
    fn execute<F>(&self, op: F) -> Result<&'static str, CallError>
    where F: FnMut(u32) -> Result<&'static str, CallError> { todo!() }
}


fn main() {
    let policy = RetryPolicy {
        max_attempts: 4,
        base_delay_ms: 100,
        max_delay_ms: 1000,
        budget_ms: 10_000,
    };
    assert_eq!(policy.next_delay(0), Some(100));
    assert_eq!(policy.next_delay(1), Some(200));
    assert_eq!(policy.next_delay(2), Some(400));
    assert_eq!(policy.next_delay(3), None); // attempt 3 is last try

    // Succeeds on 3rd try
    let mut n = 0;
    let r = policy.execute(|_a| {
        n += 1;
        if n < 3 {
            Err(CallError::Timeout)
        } else {
            Ok("ok")
        }
    });
    assert_eq!(r, Ok("ok"));
    assert_eq!(n, 3);

    // Fatal is not retried
    let mut n2 = 0;
    let r2 = policy.execute(|_| {
        n2 += 1;
        Err(CallError::Fatal)
    });
    assert_eq!(r2, Err(CallError::Fatal));
    assert_eq!(n2, 1);

    // Budget stops retries early
    let tight = RetryPolicy {
        max_attempts: 10,
        base_delay_ms: 500,
        max_delay_ms: 500,
        budget_ms: 600, // only one 500ms delay fits
    };
    let mut n3 = 0;
    let r3 = tight.execute(|_| {
        n3 += 1;
        Err(CallError::Unavailable)
    });
    assert_eq!(r3, Err(CallError::Unavailable));
    assert_eq!(n3, 2); // initial + one retry

    println!("W98 ok");
}
Full solution key — reveal after candidate finishes 
#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
struct RetryPolicy {
    max_attempts: u32,
    base_delay_ms: u64,
    max_delay_ms: u64,
    /// Total retry delay budget across attempts (not including call time).
    budget_ms: u64,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
enum CallError {
    Timeout,
    Unavailable,
    Fatal,
}

impl CallError {
    fn retryable(self) -> bool {
        matches!(self, CallError::Timeout | CallError::Unavailable)
    }
}

impl RetryPolicy {
    fn next_delay(&self, attempt: u32) -> Option<u64> {
        // attempt is 0-based index of the *retry* after a failure (0 = first retry)
        if attempt + 1 >= self.max_attempts {
            return None; // no more retries (max_attempts includes the initial try)
        }
        let exp = self
            .base_delay_ms
            .saturating_mul(1u64 << attempt.min(20));
        Some(exp.min(self.max_delay_ms))
    }

    /// Simulate calling `op` with per-attempt timeout classification.
    fn execute<F>(&self, mut op: F) -> Result<&'static str, CallError>
    where
        F: FnMut(u32) -> Result<&'static str, CallError>,
    {
        let mut spent_delay = 0u64;
        for attempt in 0..self.max_attempts {
            match op(attempt) {
                Ok(v) => return Ok(v),
                Err(e) if !e.retryable() => return Err(e),
                Err(e) => {
                    if let Some(d) = self.next_delay(attempt) {
                        if spent_delay + d > self.budget_ms {
                            return Err(e); // budget exhausted
                        }
                        spent_delay += d;
                    } else {
                        return Err(e);
                    }
                }
            }
        }
        Err(CallError::Unavailable)
    }
}

fn main() {
    let policy = RetryPolicy {
        max_attempts: 4,
        base_delay_ms: 100,
        max_delay_ms: 1000,
        budget_ms: 10_000,
    };
    assert_eq!(policy.next_delay(0), Some(100));
    assert_eq!(policy.next_delay(1), Some(200));
    assert_eq!(policy.next_delay(2), Some(400));
    assert_eq!(policy.next_delay(3), None); // attempt 3 is last try

    // Succeeds on 3rd try
    let mut n = 0;
    let r = policy.execute(|_a| {
        n += 1;
        if n < 3 {
            Err(CallError::Timeout)
        } else {
            Ok("ok")
        }
    });
    assert_eq!(r, Ok("ok"));
    assert_eq!(n, 3);

    // Fatal is not retried
    let mut n2 = 0;
    let r2 = policy.execute(|_| {
        n2 += 1;
        Err(CallError::Fatal)
    });
    assert_eq!(r2, Err(CallError::Fatal));
    assert_eq!(n2, 1);

    // Budget stops retries early
    let tight = RetryPolicy {
        max_attempts: 10,
        base_delay_ms: 500,
        max_delay_ms: 500,
        budget_ms: 600, // only one 500ms delay fits
    };
    let mut n3 = 0;
    let r3 = tight.execute(|_| {
        n3 += 1;
        Err(CallError::Unavailable)
    });
    assert_eq!(r3, Err(CallError::Unavailable));
    assert_eq!(n3, 2); // initial + one retry

    println!("W98 ok");
}
What to look for — unprompted signals
  • ★★★Retryable vs fatal classification — Fatal never retries.
  • ★★★Budget + max_attempts both bound work — not infinite backoff.
  • ★★Exponential delay capped at max_delay.
  • ★Mentions jitter (W92) and idempotency requirements for safe retries.
Follow-up probes
  • P1"Is Timeout always retryable?" — Often yes for reads; for non-idempotent writes only with idempotency keys.
  • P2"Client vs server retry budgets?" — Shared budgets prevent retry storms amplifying outages (adaptive concurrency).
  • P3"Where does deadline go?" — Overall deadline should shorten per-attempt timeouts so total stays bounded.
🎯 Senior angle
Retries without budgets and error classification cause outage amplification. Seniors separate Fatal from Timeout, cap delay, and talk about idempotency before they write the loop.
